text: September payrolls came in at just 29,000 jobs (far below the 84,000 forecast) while inflation jumped to 3.7% on an energy surge — this stagflationary mix of weakening jobs and rising prices with a Fed expected to hike again in December means you should be cautious about adding new risk right now.

QBTS is down 60% from its high with no earnings, a quarter of its shares being bet against it by short sellers, and insiders dumping stock — the thesis is broken and this should be sold to stop further damage.

IONQ is down 56% with negative earnings, cash-burning operations, 12% short interest, and insider selling — quantum computing is exciting long-term but this stock is telling you the market doesn't believe yet, so exit now.

RGTI is down 73% from its high with shrinking revenue (down 34%), no profits, heavy insider selling, and 21% short interest — this is the most damaged position in the portfolio and should be sold immediately.

MSTR is down 49% with deeply negative cash flow and insider selling — it's essentially a leveraged Bitcoin bet, so reduce your position size to limit the outsized damage it can do if crypto weakens further.

Adobe at a PE of 9 with a 10% free cash flow yield (meaning it generates a lot of real cash relative to its price) and steady 10% revenue growth looks genuinely undervalued — consider adding on this pullback.
Google under a PE of 19 with 15% revenue growth and strong cash flow is cheap by its own historical standards — this is a high-quality name worth adding to at these levels.
Micron's 256% revenue growth driven by AI demand at a PE of just 4.5 with strong free cash flow makes this a compelling add, though be aware semiconductor stocks can be cyclical.
